appraisal_events.evidence: « On ne me permet pas de jouer avec des Israélites », disait Albertine. La façon dont elle prononçait « issraêlite »... aurait suffi à indiquer... que ce n'était pas de sentiments de sympathie envers le peuple élu qu'étaient animées ces jeunes bourgeoises... et qui devaient croire aisément que les Juifs égorgeaient les enfants chrétiens; ... « Comme tout ce qui touche à la tribu », répondait Albertine sur le ton sentencieux d'une personne d'expérience.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator dissects Albertine's mispronunciation and sententious tone to expose casual, unreflective antisemitic prejudice beneath her air of worldly assurance, locally diminishing her through direct ironic commentary rather than neutral report.

status_effects.explanation: Albertine's remarks about the Bloch sisters are unmasked by the narrator as prejudiced rather than merely socially discerning, lowering her standing in the narration.

Andrée's parallel dismissal of the Bloch sisters ('un sale genre') places her alongside Albertine in the same narratorially exposed prejudice, though she receives less direct narratorial unpacking than Albertine.

ambiguities: The narrator's critique of antisemitic prejudice is phrased as applying broadly to 'ces jeunes bourgeoises' (Albertine's circle of friends, presumably including Andrée), not solely to Albertine individually, though she alone receives extended narratorial commentary; Andrée's parallel remark is treated here as part of the same local movement rather than a fully distinct event.
